clue.text: Fish get into difficulties

definitions.meaning: a flatfish of that name, a common table fish
to struggle clumsily, as a swimmer out of their depth or a nervous speaker does

explanation.surface: An angler or a fish in trouble, read as a plain instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a flatfish and also means to struggle or stumble helplessly, so both senses fit.

clue.text: Little bit of Africa to investigate, travelling north

indicators.note: travelling north says the hidden letters are read backwards
a bit of something is a part taken from it, so the letters lie within the following words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An expedition heads north to look into a small part of Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'travelling north' means reading upwards, so the letters spanning 'Africa to investigate' are taken bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek letter's name is used idiomatically for a tiny amount, as in 'not one jot or tittle'.

clue.text: Draw spirit miles up

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means the pieces are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: an elf is a small mischievous spirit
miles, as in 'miles better', means far

explanation.surface: Someone sketches a spirit rising many miles into the air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns ELFFAR (ELF then FAR) upside down in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A raffle is a lottery in which tickets are drawn, so a draw is a synonym.

clue.text: Fish ball with different starter

indicators.note: a different starter means the first letter of the word for ball is swapped for another

parts.note: a bollock is British slang for a testicle, a ball

explanation.surface: A fishball made to a different recipe at the start of a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: BOLLOCK is vulgar British slang for a testicle; 'with different starter' swaps its B for P.
explanation.definitionFit: The pollock is a North Atlantic food fish related to the cod.

clue.text: Contemporary scholar gathering speed

indicators.note: gathering means the word for scholar collects the other piece inside it

parts.note: a sage is a wise, learned person
pace means speed or rate

explanation.surface: A modern academic picks up the pace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gathering' reads as a scholar collecting momentum, but it signals one piece held inside the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Space-age describes something very modern or up to date, hence contemporary.

clue.text: Temporary office left, using this handle over ditch

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece placed over another means it comes before it

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship
aka, 'also known as', is what introduces a handle or alias
to bin something is to ditch or throw it away

explanation.surface: An office worker leaves, giving an alias, after something was dumped in a ditch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'handle' is slang for a name; AKA is the abbreviation used when giving one.
explanation.definitionFit: A Portakabin is a British brand of portable prefabricated building, often used as a site office.

clue.text: Drinking litres, bum virtually drunk

indicators.note: drinking means the trimmed word swallows the other piece
virtually means almost all, so the final letter is lost

parts.note: bum is British slang for the bottom

explanation.surface: A drinker downing litres is nearly drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'virtually' trims BOTTOM to BOTTO, and 'Drinking' puts L inside it after the B.
explanation.definitionFit: Blotto is informal for extremely intoxicated, a synonym of drunk.

clue.text: Rich source, fish served with last drops of sardine oil

indicators.note: the last drops of each word are their final letters

parts.note: the dorado is a fish, also called mahi-mahi

explanation.surface: A fish served with sardine oil dregs makes a lavish dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last drops of' takes the final letters E and L of 'sardine' and 'oil', which come first.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary city of gold, a byword for any place offering great wealth or opportunity.

clue.text: Stick securing old, hollowed out puppet

indicators.note: securing means the stick holds the other piece within it

parts.note: a pole is a long stick

indicators.note: hollowed out leaves only the outer letters of the word

explanation.surface: A stick holds up an old puppet with its stuffing removed.
explanation.walkthrough: A poodle is a political lapdog, so 'puppet' is a fair definition rather than a marionette.
explanation.definitionFit: A poodle is figuratively a servile follower controlled by another, a political puppet.

clue.text: Fish, a freak doing the backstroke?

indicators.note: swimming backwards means the words are read in reverse

parts.note: a nut is an enthusiast or freak, as in health nut

explanation.surface: Asks whether a fish is some oddball swimming on its back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doing the backstroke' reverses A NUT.
explanation.definitionFit: Tuna is a large ocean fish of the mackerel family.

clue.text: In death, evoke praise

indicators.note: in means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: fate can mean death or ruin, as in 'met his fate'
to elicit is to draw out or evoke a response

explanation.surface: A eulogy drawing out praise for the dead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' is the container signal, putting the word for evoke inside the word for death.
explanation.definitionFit: To felicitate is to congratulate, which is to commend or compliment someone.

clue.text: OK to put away bed and lie around?

indicators.note: around means the letters are scattered and turned about into a new order

explanation.surface: Asks whether it is fine to tidy away the bed and laze about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put away' is slang for eat, not tidy up; 'around' signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that is fit to eat is safe to 'put away', slang for consume.

clue.text: Ladies scantily dressed, Barbra Streisand's initials covering her topless picture

indicators.note: covering means the initials sit around the other piece
initials are the first letters of the two names
topless means the first letter is removed

parts.note: Funny Girl is the 1968 film, her picture, that made Streisand a screen star

explanation.surface: Racy chorus girls, with a Streisand monogram over a nude poster of her.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topless' drops the film title's first letter, and 'covering' wraps the singer's initials round what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Playboy club waitresses wore skimpy costumes with rabbit ears and tails.

clue.text: Two things smoked, queer fish

parts.note: the clue's 'two things smoked' are a pair of drugs; the first is crack cocaine
the second thing smoked is pot, slang for cannabis

explanation.surface: Smoking two substances is what an eccentric does.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two things smoked' covers both halves at once: crack cocaine and pot, each smoked.
explanation.definitionFit: A queer fish is an idiom for an odd person; a crank or eccentric is a synonym.

clue.text: My Lord has invested currency — big fish

indicators.note: invested means clothed, so the exclamation wraps round the money

parts.note: gee is an exclamation of surprise, like 'My Lord!'
the rand is South Africa's currency

explanation.surface: A peer has put money into a major investment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My Lord' looks like a peer's form of address but is just an exclamation; 'has invested' means clothes, so wraps round.
explanation.definitionFit: A grandee is a person of high rank; a big fish is idiom for an important person.

clue.text: Realisation, where I happen to change personality, ultimately

indicators.note: change means the letters are altered into a new order
ultimately takes the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A sudden realisation that brings a change of personality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to change' rearranges I HAPPEN into EPIPHAN; 'ultimately' adds Y from 'personality'.
explanation.definitionFit: An epiphany is a sudden moment of insight or understanding, a realisation.

clue.text: Deep, deep fish

parts.note: the deep is a poetic name for the sea
a deep voice is a bass one

explanation.surface: A fish from the ocean depths.
explanation.walkthrough: The repeated word is taken in two senses: the ocean, then low in pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: The sea bass is a marine food fish, so it is an example of a fish.

clue.text: Fish is covered in cream after gutting error

parts.note: the sole is a flatfish

indicators.note: covered in means the second word is wrapped by the gutted letters
gutting removes the insides, leaving only the outer letters

explanation.surface: A fish dish in a cream sauce, with a cooking mistake in gutting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after gutting' empties 'cream' to its outer letters, and 'covered in' wraps them round 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A solecism is a grammatical mistake or breach of etiquette, a type of error.

clue.text: V fishy stain under unopened receptacle

indicators.note: in a down clue, under means this piece comes below the other
unopened means the first letter is taken away

parts.note: a bag is a receptacle for carrying things

indicators.note: fishy means suspect or odd, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A fishy stain found under a sealed bag, perhaps evidence in a case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unopened' cuts BAG to AG; 'fishy' rearranges STAIN to AINST, placed 'under' it.
explanation.definitionFit: V stands for versus, Latin for against, as in a contest between sides.

clue.text: Fish good with two fish

parts.note: the ray and the ling are both fish

explanation.surface: A tasty fish served with two others.
explanation.definitionFit: The grayling is a freshwater fish of the salmon family.

clue.text: Kipper in front, farewell forever seafood sandwiches!

indicators.note: sandwiches means the two outer pieces enclose the other

parts.note: RIP, rest in peace, is a final farewell
a winkle is an edible sea snail
the van is the front, as in vanguard

explanation.surface: A kipper is set out front with a goodbye to seafood sandwiches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kipper' looks like the smoked fish but means one who kips, sleeps.
explanation.definitionFit: The Washington Irving character slept for twenty years, the ultimate sleeper.

clue.text: See 21
Come to understand thread about European Union

indicators.note: about means the first piece goes round the second

parts.note: a wisp is a thin thread of smoke or hair

explanation.surface: Understanding, at last, a thread of discussion about the EU.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thread' suggests a discussion thread, but it is a wisp of smoke or hair; 'about' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: To wise up is an idiom meaning to become aware of the truth of something.

clue.text: Croatian boxers reportedly bringing carp

parts.note: Split is a port city in Croatia

indicators.note: reportedly means the word is as it is said aloud, not spelt

parts.note: hares are known for boxing in spring

explanation.surface: A Croatian boxing match attracts a bit of fishing.
explanation.walkthrough: Hares box each other upright in the mating season; HARES said aloud gives HAIRS.
explanation.definitionFit: To carp is to quibble pettily; splitting hairs is the idiom for petty distinctions.

clue.text: Stonefish?

parts.note: split in two, the word asks for something that is both a stone and a fish

explanation.surface: A query about a venomous fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stonefish' looks like the venomous reef fish, but read as stone plus fish: rock is stone, and British chip shops sell dogfish as rock salmon.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a synonym of stone, and in British fish-and-chip shops it names dogfish sold as rock salmon.

clue.text: Fish bleeding briefly

indicators.note: briefly means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: bleeding and ruddy are both mild British intensifiers, as in 'ruddy cheek'

explanation.surface: A fish is bleeding for a short while.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' cuts RUDDY to RUDD.
explanation.definitionFit: The rudd is a European freshwater fish of the carp family.

clue.text: Fish not a sausage male's thrown back

indicators.note: thrown back means read backwards, like a fish returned to the water

parts.note: British slang for nothing at all, so nil
a ram is a male sheep; the 's is a linking 'is'

explanation.surface: No fish at all: the male catch has been thrown back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thrown back' reverses NILRAM; 'not a sausage' is British slang for nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: The marlin is a large ocean game fish with a spear-like snout.

clue.text: Transport used on street, most reliable

indicators.note: to transport is to carry away, so the letters are moved into a new order

explanation.surface: The most reliable transport is used on the street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Transport' reads as a noun but rearranges USED ON into SOUNDE.
explanation.definitionFit: Sound means reliable or solid, as in sound advice; the superlative means most reliable.
